neighbours.label: the second small piece of a short split word or name: reduplicated interjections and short names (Nuh-uh, yo-yo, SoLa, Yuja, Noa)
fire: When the teacher asked if he had finished, the boy just shook his head and said uh-uh.
My niece got a shiny red yo-yo for her birthday and played with it all day.
The small bakery Mimi & Lulu opened a second shop downtown.
Last night the cellist Yoyo Ma joined the orchestra for an encore.
The toddler waved and shouted bye-bye to the mail carrier.
Her golden retriever, named Kiki, refuses to walk in the rain.
The new café NoHo Brew serves coffee until midnight.
He answered every question with a cheerful uh-huh and kept typing.
quiet: When the teacher asked if he had finished, the boy just shook his head and said nothing.
My niece got a shiny red bicycle for her birthday and played with it all day.
The small bakery on Main Street opened a second shop downtown.
Last night the famous cellist joined the orchestra for an encore.
The toddler waved and shouted goodbye to the mail carrier.
Her golden retriever, named Charlie, refuses to walk in the rain.
The new café on the corner serves coffee until midnight.
He answered every question with a cheerful nod and kept typing.

short: second piece of short split name
notes: Card: top examples are 'uh' in 'Nuh-uh', 'La' in 'SoLa', 'a' in 'Noa', 'ja' in 'Yuja', 'L' in 'LaLone', '-y' in 'yo-yo' - the second tiny token of a short word that the tokenizer splits. Probe: these five 0.57-0.96; an ordinary pianist name 0.02. (I first mislabeled the - pole by mistake; this entry is for the drawn + pole.)
